_comment: Hand-maintained mapping from what the pricing page shows to what the API calls things.
Nothing here is inferred at runtime: no fuzzy matching, no lowercasing and hoping.
'page_name' is compared byte-for-byte against the data-name attribute of the model
card, and 'label' byte-for-byte against the row label inside that card. A page that
no longer contains these exact strings is a failure to report, never a row to guess at.
The keys of 'models' are API model ids. Several of them are ALIASES: today
mistral-medium-latest resolves to Mistral Medium 3.5, tomorrow it will resolve to
something else at a different price, with no change anywhere in this file. That is
precisely why the resolution is written down here by a human and revisited by a human.
Last verified against the page by a human: 2026-08-03.
_comment_voxtral: ASSUMPTION, revisit it. Both rows of the 'voxtral small' card carry the same
parenthetical, '(per min / per M tok)', and neither says which of the two units
applies to it. Reading the audio row as per-minute and the text row as per-M-token
is the sensible interpretation, and it is only an interpretation. It is written
down here, rather than inferred in code, so that a human can check it.
Note also that 'voxtral small' is billed in BOTH units at once: per minute of
audio in and per million tokens of text. Any code assuming one unit per model
Decoy on the page: 'voxtral mini transcribe realtime' carries a row labelled
